message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the development of a mane in adult males. The presence of a mane is controlled by a dominant allele (often referred to as “M”) that masks the recessive allele (“m”) responsible for a lack of mane. Thus, when a male lion inherits at least one copy of the dominant allele from either parent, it will develop a mane.
